correctness.rationale: Select finite matrix tuples \(X^{(r)}\) with \(\|X^{(r)}\|_{\mathcal E_1}=1\) and \(\|X^{(r)}\|_{\mathcal E_2}\to c\) by the cb-norm definition. Tornes Theorem 3.1 was read in full: for each input \(X\) its constructed \(T_X\) has exactly the \(m\)-th Haagerup and minimal word-operator norms \(\|X\|_{\mathcal E}^m\), all \(m\ge1\), not merely an asymptotic statement. The coordinate operators of \(T_X\) are shifted tensor placements of input coordinates, so have norm exactly \(\|X_j\|\). Each coordinate functional on fixed finite-dimensional \(\mathcal E_1\) is bounded/completely bounded, uniformly bounding \(\|X_j^{(r)}\|\). Their countable direct sum \(T_j=\oplus_r(T_{X^{(r)}})_j\) therefore exists and is bounded on separable \(K\); the words are block diagonal and their norms equal the supremum of the corresponding block word norms. Taking roots at every power gives both radii \(\sup_r\|X^{(r)}\|_{\mathcal E}\), proving the exact requested values. No finite-level norm attainment was assumed.

evidence: Theorem 3.1 supplies the exact all-powers encoding lemma, requiring a separate countable norming-sequence construction to realize \(c\).
Corollary 3.3 yields a yes/no complete-isometry test, not an attained cb-distortion value.

value.rationale: The completely bounded norm is the canonical quantitative distortion invariant of operator-space quantizations. Realizing an otherwise unattained supremum over all finite levels as exact simultaneous ordinary/minimal spectral radii of one separable tuple is a natural attainment statement usable to compare operator-space structures; no general downstream theorem is needed.

final_claim: For finite-dimensional operator-space structures \(\mathcal E_1,\mathcal E_2\) on \(\mathbb C^d\), \(d\ge1\), let \(c=\|\mathrm{id}:\mathcal E_1\to\mathcal E_2\|_{\mathrm{cb}}\). There is one bounded operator \(d\)-tuple on a separable Hilbert space with \(\rho_{\mathcal E_1}(T)=\rho^{\min}_{\mathcal E_1}(T)=1\) and \(\rho_{\mathcal E_2}(T)=\rho^{\min}_{\mathcal E_2}(T)=c\), even if no finite matrix level attains \(c\).
limitations: The witness is generally infinite dimensional; finite-matrix or universal-pair-independent attainment is not claimed.
The order of the two operator-space structures matters, and separability follows from a countable sequence of finite-dimensional inputs.
